paper_title: Torsion-balance tests of the weak equivalence principle
notes: Eot-Wash rotating torsion balance (Be-Ti, Be-Al) WEP test. Headline exotic-force result is Figure 6 left panel: the 95% CL curve labeled 'EW' (this paper's lab-fixed result from Table 3, propagated through a geophysical Earth model), the deepest/lowest blue curve; the EW94, EW99, Princeton, Moscow and LLR curves are prior experiments and were not used. The plane is a vector Yukawa force coupled to q=N=B-L (i.e. U(1)_{B-L} boson), so reported as VectorBL. Extracted by parsing the vector EPS (WEP_figure6.eps) into colored polylines; axes calibrated from the frame box x=[1e-2,1e12] m (log) and y=|alpha|=[1e-11,1e-5] (log). The paper plots the Yukawa strength relative to gravity alpha_tilde = g^2/(4*pi*G*u^2) (eqs 2,4). Converted to the gauge coupling via g_BL = sqrt(4*pi*alpha_tilde)*u/M_Pl with u=0.931494 GeV, M_Pl=1.2209e19 GeV (G=1/M_Pl^2 natural units); K=sqrt(4pi)*u/M_Pl=2.705e-19, so g_BL=K*sqrt(alpha_tilde). x converted from range lambda via m=1.97327e-7 eV*m/lambda. Flat long-range (small mass) plateau alpha~3e-11 gives g_BL~1.48e-24; limit weakens (g_BL up to ~9e-22) at short range (large mass, lambda~0.2 m) where the curve exits the top of the plot at alpha=1e-5. Curve collapsed with RDP in log-log; the large mass gap between the first two points is the genuine flat plateau. Limit is not dark-matter-density dependent.
